comment: Android's hardware codecs (CodecBridge, MediaCodec c2.qti.*) for the Linux side's GStreamer and FFmpeg adapters, through their shared transport shared/media/codec-client.c. A binary protocol, not JSON lines: every number a big-endian 32-bit word (pts: two words, high first). The broker socket /mnt/android-wayland/codec.sock takes MAGIC once, then OPEN per codec; for each it answers CHANNEL with two descriptors (SCM_RIGHTS): a channel socket and shared memory of two halves of HALF bytes (input in the first, output in the second), or ERROR when all codec slots are taken. On the channel: the consumer sends `configure`; the provider answers DONE and the codec's name (`configured`) or ERROR, a length and a message (`error`). Then commands: FRAME with `frame` (the input in the first half), DRAIN, FLUSH or CLOSE; the provider answers any number of `output` records (each acknowledged with ACK; the output in the second half: compressed data, or a decoded picture's three planes one after another with their row stride, pixel step and length, which may overlap as in Android's semi-planar images), EOS after a drain, and DONE. kind: 0 H.264, 1 HEVC, 2 VP9 (decode only); encoder input is I420 of width*height*3/2 bytes. Channel version 2 (CodecBridge since APK 2.33): `configure2` starts with MAGIC2 and adds options (OPTION_BUFFERS: decoded pictures stay in the decoder's own buffers; OPTION_TEN_BIT: 10-bit pictures as P010), and every record is an `output2`: three plane offsets, a buffer (-1: the output half of the shared memory, as before; else the slot of one of the decoder's buffers) and the depth (8, or 10 for P010). A picture in a slot arrives with the slot's DMA-BUF attached (SCM_RIGHTS on the record's first byte) the first time the slot appears; size is then the buffer's length and the offsets are from its start; the consumer maps it, brackets its reads with DMA_BUF_IOCTL_SYNC and keeps it until the channel closes; slot numbers only grow (a new buffer set gets new ones). The app holds the picture until the ACK. An app before version 2 answers MAGIC2 with ERROR (Channel version): the consumer then uses version 1. Every exchange opens Android's hardware codec, so there is no read-only query: the provider side is acceptance codec.hw (an H.264 encode and decode through the GStreamer and FFmpeg adapters on the phone). Consumer side: tools/tests/test_contract_codec.py (the real codec-client.c, built here, against tools/contracts.py's CodecStandIn).
